chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a bleacher to whom I had handed over a garment, and he claimed that it had been stolen from among his goods. He said: 'So upon him is that he establishes proof that it was stolen from among his goods, and there is nothing upon him. And if all his goods were stolen, there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ: There is nothing upon him (exempt from liability)
key_terms.قَصَّارٍ: Bleacher (a type of bailee who processes fabrics)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal liability of a bailee if their stored goods are stolen?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a bailee (qassār) is exempt from compensation if they prove the goods were stolen from their possession, shifting the burden of proof to the owner to demonstrate negligence or breach of trust. This principle underscores the Shia legal concept of 'presumption of innocence' (al-asl al-salamah) in commercial transactions, where liability is not automatic but contingent upon verified fault. The hadith highlights the importance of evidentiary standards in Islamic jurisprudence to protect merchants from unjust claims.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a bleacher to whom some clothes had been handed over, and there was an allegation that he had stolen from between his goods. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So upon him (owner) is that he has to establish proof that he (bleacher) has stolen from between his goods, and there is nothing upon him (the bleacher to establish) and even if all of his goods had been stolen, so there would be nothing upon him’.
